case.question: Give us a 30-day launch marketing plan for each city: Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
expected: Proposed metrics rather than promised results

answer.headline: 30-day launch plan: same core meaty-pizza/kebab offer, Dubai weighted to delivery-app visibility, Abu Dhabi weighted to sampling and event-adjacent tie-ins; all figures are proposals to be costed and measured.

items.text: Both cities are planning assumptions only; the profile has no set city weighting, branch format, or audience, so treat the plan as a template that a site decision must precede. Suggest /set branch_format and positioning so the plan can be narrowed.

Food photography and short vertical video of the meaty pizza slice-pull and kebab sandwich build are the primary creative assets for both cities; the same pack can be reused across channels and both cities, which keeps production cost per asset down.

For paid visibility inside the app, Deliveroo advertises native Marketer Adverts, promotional offers such as free delivery and BOGOF, and partner performance insights to UAE merchants; eligibility at a specific address must be confirmed with the provider before budgeting.

Week 1 test: one hero bundle per city on the delivery app plus in-store, priced against the observed Papa Johns UAE anchors of AED 37 (small 8-inch pizza, potato wedges, canned drink) and AED 69 (medium pizza, two starters, two canned drinks); the bundle price is a proposal to be validated against our own food cost, not an observed range for our concept.

Dubai: shift spend into app discovery plus late-evening daypart tests, using Marketer Adverts and a limited-time free-delivery or BOGOF slot on one or two items only, with the discount cost per order tracked separately from ad spend.

Dubai competitive context: Allo Beirut lists a Hessa Street branch in Al Barsha and advertises delivery until 4 AM; that is a branch and hours listing only — it does not establish overnight demand or the catchment available to our site, so late-night hours should be tested, not assumed.

Packaging must satisfy Dubai Municipality delivery guidance: sealed containers, hot/cold separation in insulated secondary units, and transport holding at 60 C or above for hot food; build this into the launch checklist before day 1 rather than after first complaints.

sections.title: Days 21-30: Abu Dhabi activation and measurement

items.text: Abu Dhabi: pair app visibility with physical sampling near a chosen site, since the DCT 2025 figure of 252 culture and leisure events with over 4.2 million attendees is emirate-level and historical and cannot be read as footfall or demand at any specific location.

Abu Dhabi menu framing should lean on sandwich and kebab language: Talabat lists Operation Falafel in Madinat Khalifa A under Arabic, Lebanese, sandwich, shawarma and falafel categories, indicating that sandwich/shawarma terminology is used in that delivery market; this is one branch listing and does not show category gaps or demand.

Measurement: fix simple targets before spending — offer redemptions, new-versus-returning customers, orders per rider slot, and contribution after discount per order. Deliveroo advertises partner insights, but this is an advertised feature, not confirmed access to a dataset; verify access with the account manager.

Delivery structure choice for both cities: compare platform rider network versus Marketplace+ own-rider model, which advertises selectable delivery area, minimum spend and delivery fees alongside an option to request a platform rider; neither commission nor fees are verified, so request written terms for the specific address.

assumptions: Budget, rent budget, branch format, target audience, positioning and opening date are all unset in the profile, so no spend level or city weighting is assumed here.
The concept stays meaty pizza plus kebab sandwiches in both cities, and any bundle priced around the cited Papa Johns anchors must be validated against our own food cost before launch.
next_steps: Confirm the delivery partner terms for the exact proposed address in each city — commission, fees, delivery area, minimum spend, and whether Marketer Adverts and promotions are available there.
Cost one hero bundle and one single-item offer per city, including packaging and any discount funding, then set a maximum acceptable discount per order before launch.

Choose the Abu Dhabi sampling location and Dubai delivery focus area from site checks (visibility, parking, rider access, competitor presence nearby) rather than from city-level event or tourism figures.
Run the first 30 days with a single measurement sheet covering redemptions, repeat rate and contribution after discount, then decide which channel gets month-two spend.

**Days 1-10: foundations both cities**

- **Assumption:** Both cities are planning assumptions only; the profile has no set city weighting, branch format, or audience, so treat the plan as a template that a site decision must precede. Suggest /set branch\_format and positioning so the plan can be narrowed.
- **Proposal:** Food photography and short vertical video of the meaty pizza slice-pull and kebab sandwich build are the primary creative assets for both cities; the same pack can be reused across channels and both cities, which keeps production cost per asset down.
- **Fact:** For paid visibility inside the app, Deliveroo advertises native Marketer Adverts, promotional offers such as free delivery and BOGOF, and partner performance insights to UAE merchants; eligibility at a specific address must be confirmed with the provider before budgeting. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/why-deliveroo/growth>)
- **Proposal:** Week 1 test: one hero bundle per city on the delivery app plus in-store, priced against the observed Papa Johns UAE anchors of AED 37 \(small 8-inch pizza, potato wedges, canned drink\) and AED 69 \(medium pizza, two starters, two canned drinks\); the bundle price is a proposal to be validated against our own food cost, not an observed range for our concept. [2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/menu>)

**Days 11-20: Dubai activation**

- **Proposal:** Dubai: shift spend into app discovery plus late-evening daypart tests, using Marketer Adverts and a limited-time free-delivery or BOGOF slot on one or two items only, with the discount cost per order tracked separately from ad spend. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/why-deliveroo/growth>)
- **Fact:** Dubai competitive context: Allo Beirut lists a Hessa Street branch in Al Barsha and advertises delivery until 4 AM; that is a branch and hours listing only — it does not establish overnight demand or the catchment available to our site, so late-night hours should be tested, not assumed. [3](<https://www.allobeirutstreetfood.com/locations>)
- **Fact:** Packaging must satisfy Dubai Municipality delivery guidance: sealed containers, hot/cold separation in insulated secondary units, and transport holding at 60 C or above for hot food; build this into the launch checklist before day 1 rather than after first complaints. [4](<https://dmpmedia.dm.gov.ae/uploads/2024/02/2.-DM-FSD-GU63-Requirements-for-food-transportation-and-delivery-vehicles-guidelines-update.pdf>)

**Days 21-30: Abu Dhabi activation and measurement**

- **Fact:** Abu Dhabi: pair app visibility with physical sampling near a chosen site, since the DCT 2025 figure of 252 culture and leisure events with over 4.2 million attendees is emirate-level and historical and cannot be read as footfall or demand at any specific location. [5](<https://www.mediaoffice.abudhabi/en/tourism/abu-dhabis-culture-and-tourism-sectors-delivered-strong-growth-in-2025-with-26m-visitors/>)
- **Fact:** Abu Dhabi menu framing should lean on sandwich and kebab language: Talabat lists Operation Falafel in Madinat Khalifa A under Arabic, Lebanese, sandwich, shawarma and falafel categories, indicating that sandwich/shawarma terminology is used in that delivery market; this is one branch listing and does not show category gaps or demand. [6](<https://www.talabat.com/uae/restaurant/704423/operation-falafel-khalifa-city--ad-7?aid=1483>)
- **Proposal:** Measurement: fix simple targets before spending — offer redemptions, new-versus-returning customers, orders per rider slot, and contribution after discount per order. Deliveroo advertises partner insights, but this is an advertised feature, not confirmed access to a dataset; verify access with the account manager. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/why-deliveroo/growth>)
- **Fact:** Delivery structure choice for both cities: compare platform rider network versus Marketplace+ own-rider model, which advertises selectable delivery area, minimum spend and delivery fees alongside an option to request a platform rider; neither commission nor fees are verified, so request written terms for the specific address. [7](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [8](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>)

**Assumptions and limitations**

- Budget, rent budget, branch format, target audience, positioning and opening date are all unset in the profile, so no spend level or city weighting is assumed here.
- The concept stays meaty pizza plus kebab sandwiches in both cities, and any bundle priced around the cited Papa Johns anchors must be validated against our own food cost before launch.

**Next steps**

- Confirm the delivery partner terms for the exact proposed address in each city — commission, fees, delivery area, minimum spend, and whether Marketer Adverts and promotions are available there.
- Cost one hero bundle and one single-item offer per city, including packaging and any discount funding, then set a maximum acceptable discount per order before launch.
- Choose the Abu Dhabi sampling location and Dubai delivery focus area from site checks \(visibility, parking, rider access, competitor presence nearby\) rather than from city-level event or tourism figures.
- Run the first 30 days with a single measurement sheet covering redemptions, repeat rate and contribution after discount, then decide which channel gets month-two spend.
